prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of GLP-1 physiology and the active incretin peptide that enabled a new class of therapies for type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: After reading the full first-round exchange, my preferred configuration is unchanged: B035 alone, credited to Holst, Drucker and Mojsov. The scientific case does not depend on how many of us ranked it first. It is a complete and independently confirmed chain, from the incretin effect and proglucagon processing, through the truncated active GLP-1(7-36) peptide and its glucose-dependent insulinotropic and satiety actions, to receptor biology and agonists with randomized evidence on glycaemia, weight and cardiovascular and renal outcomes. The three credited names map onto separable steps (physiology, receptor and proglucagon biology, the active peptide), which is the cleanest allocation available on this shortlist and keeps the emphasis on discovery. No member raised a maturity objection, and I see none.
statement.case_against: Attribution is still the weak point, and the exchange has sharpened it rather than resolved it. Mojsov's priority on the active peptide relative to Habener and colleagues is contested, and no one has yet verified the record. Knudsen, whose work on acylated long-acting analogues produced the drugs that reached patients, is excluded by the three-person cap, so a discovery-centred citation can be read as honouring the physiology while leaving out the medicine. If the committee concludes that the therapeutic step is inseparable from the discovery, my configuration would be too narrow, and I would then prefer to accept Knudsen in place of Mojsov rather than in place of Holst. I would not take that step on an unverified doubt about Mojsov.

responses.point: Perlmann argues that the citation should be explicitly about the hormone and its active form, which defensibly keeps Knudsen out, and asks that the secretariat verify the historical record on the active peptide before the final ballot. He ranks TNF blockade (B002) below CAR-T because its discernible change happened long ago.
responses.response: I now agree with him more than in round 1 on the citation. Writing it around the hormone and its active form makes the exclusion of Knudsen a coherent decision and not an oversight, and I have kept that wording. I share his demand for verification, and I would make the final vote conditional on it: if the record shows that Mojsov's identification of the active form was not independent or distinct, the third name should be reconsidered. On B002 I accept his point that long establishment cannot lift it above B035. I still do not read age as a mark against it, but I have not moved it ahead of CAR-T.

responses.point: Sandberg would accept Knudsen in place of Mojsov if the evidence for Mojsov's priority proves weaker than he judges it, and would pair B035 with a B029 part for June and Sadelain, accepting the loss of Mojsov or Holst from the first part. He also describes B002 as having the cleanest attribution but as a translational validation of a known cytokine.
responses.response: I agree on the conditional swap, and it is the only variant of the B035 trio I would support, because Holst's incretin physiology and Drucker's biology are the stable core. I do not support the two-part version. Giving B029 two slots would force Mojsov or Holst out of B035 and weaken the part on which we agree, to add a part whose original chimeric-receptor concept (Eshhar) we cannot credit. His question about B002 is fair: the key discovery is cytokine biology in disease, and the TNF work of Cerami, Old and Beutler and the antibody engineering both fall outside Feldmann and Maini. I concede that this weakens B002 as a lead, and it remains only an alternative, for which I repeat my disclosure of disciplinary proximity.

responses.point: The chair calls B029 the strongest challenger but says the Eshhar problem is not minor, because the credited trio emphasises clinical development and costimulation while the original chimeric-receptor concept sits outside the names. He would resist dropping Holst if Knudsen came in, and sees B002 as stronger on clinical proof of concept than on new biology.
responses.response: I accept his argument on Eshhar and now regard it as decisive against a B029 part in this configuration, not only a complication. Narrowing to June and Sadelain leaves the original concept uncredited, and keeping Rosenberg leaves it equally so. My stance on Rosenberg is therefore less important than I suggested in round 1. I agree that Holst should be the last name dropped, since the incretin effect is the oldest foundation. On B002 I partly disagree, because the shift to cytokine-directed treatment of autoimmune disease was a conceptual change as well as clinical proof, but I accept that this is not enough to put it in a prize part with B035, and I do not propose that.

uncertainties: Whether the documentary record supports Mojsov's identification of the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide as independent of and distinct from Habener-group work, and who verifies it before the final ballot.
Whether the committee will frame B035 as discovery or as drug development, which decides whether Knudsen should displace Mojsov.
Whether B029 can ever be configured cleanly without the original CAR concept (Eshhar).
Whether B002 is read as a fundamental discovery or as clinical validation, given the TNF biology (Cerami, Old, Beutler) outside the credited names.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile for B035 or B029. B002 (TNF blockade in rheumatoid arthritis) lies in my own field of rheumatology. This is disciplinary proximity, not a documented personal or institutional tie to Feldmann or Maini, and I list it only as an alternative. My profile also records a Bergen group-leader affiliation, which creates no documented tie to any credited name on the shortlist. Nothing has changed since round 1.
